acceptance: A dry run lists 3 rounds x (A cells for every version + 2.0.0 B cell + setup C cells) x benchmarks, and the count matches a formula asserted in a test

A test proves the round order is a seeded shuffle that is reproducible from the recorded seed, that each round covers every cell exactly once, and that the shuffle seed is never passed as a workload seed

A test proves the analyzer rejects a Polars cell that lacks qualification evidence or whose row counts disagree with the DuckDB reference, and accepts one with clean evidence and uncertain or not_run status
The analyzer output has median, min, max, both speedups per setup, a candidate-mover list obeying non-overlap plus the 10% effect rule, and the comparison count, checked by a fixture test

The manifest schema records versions of polars, polars-runtime-32 and pyarrow, the BenchBox commit, requested engine and collect policy, seeds, round, per-query row counts, peak RSS, swap growth and outcome class per run; the runner refuses to continue if any pinned value changes
The spec records the version list, scale factors, setups and the qualification-file SHA-256
The DuckDB spec's dry-run golden test from pvm-s3a still passes
context: 2026-10-08 (from the pvm-s0a review): BenchBox's polars-df default is rechunk=True, which Polars 1.x readers apply (the keyword is passed where accepted) but 2.0 cannot (keyword removed; platform info reports rechunk_effective=false). For a fair default-settings comparison the Polars spec must pass `--platform-option rechunk=false` on every version, so every version scans with Polars' own default (no rechunk). Record rechunk_effective per run in the manifest and assert it is false for all cells.
description:
Encode the Polars experiment in the engine-neutral tooling, with run controls and analysis rules fixed before any timed run. Merging this spec is the freeze point (D0 C7): version list, scale factors, setups, rules and the qualification/reference hashes are recorded in it, and do not change after timed data exists.

Runner (Polars spec):
- Platform polars-df. Versions and setup C membership from pvm-s1; per-benchmark scale factors and the did-not-complete list from pvm-s2.
- Setups: A = engine default on every version; B = engine in-memory on 2.0.0 only (on 1.x it is identical to A); C = engine streaming on the versions pvm-s1 admitted.
- Data: generated once, before the version loop. The pyarrow Parquet conversion is done once up front, so it is not charged to the first version.
- Workload identity (D0 C8): each measured invocation is one power run with one measurement iteration, one internal per-query warm-up (warm-per-query cache regime, replacing a separate discarded warm-up run, D0 C11/A6), the default single stream, and no workload seed (qgen default parameters). The shuffle seed is separate and only orders cells.
- Controls: POLARS_MAX_THREADS=10 (equals the Polars default on this host; recorded). POLARS_TEMP_DIR pinned under the output dir, cleaned per cell, spill bytes and free disk recorded. Three measured rounds; each round runs every cell once, in an order shuffled with a fixed seed recorded in the manifest. Before each cell: `uv pip uninstall polars polars-runtime-32`, install the cell's version from the uv cache, verify with pip freeze (D0 A3).
- Record per run: polars and polars-runtime-32 versions, requested engine and collect policy, BenchBox commit SHA, pyarrow version, host info, seeds, round index, per-query status and row counts, peak process-tree RSS, swap growth, outcome class (completed, resource-policy-exceeded, timeout, oom-killed, execution-failure; policy from pvm-s2).
- Abort the whole run if the BenchBox commit, the pyarrow version or the data changes mid-matrix.

Analyzer (Polars spec):
- Input: the manifest plus a qualification file (pvm-s1 eligibility table and pvm-s2 DuckDB reference row counts), whose SHA-256 is recorded in the spec (D0 A2).
- Accept validation statuses uncertain or not_run only when the qualification file shows clean correctness evidence for that version, setup and benchmark (cross-surface gate, TPC-H SF1 PASSED, expected query count with zero failures) AND every query's row count in the cell equals the DuckDB reference at the run's scale. Otherwise reject the cell with a reason. DuckDB keeps requiring passed.
- Every cell keeps its full-suite outcome; totals are also computed on a named common-query subset if pvm-s1 attributed a Polars defect (D0 C12).
- Report per cell the median and the min–max across the three rounds. Report speedup against the oldest admitted version and against 1.44.2, per setup.
- Candidate mover rule (D0 C4/A11): non-overlapping min–max ranges AND abs(median change) >= 10%. Report the number of comparisons made; no significance language.
- No conditional reruns: the analyzer never selects among repeated runs.

Guardrails: the decision rules above are written into code and tests before pvm-s4 runs; per handoff D3 they do not change after timed data exists — deviations are reported in pvm-s5.
